span.p: THE MACHINE THE LITERATURE ASSUMES - cited, the ladder the offload and CXL designs are built around

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: THIS MACHINE, MEASURED 2026-07-26 - Z13, gfx1151, one unified 128 GB pool, single run per arm

span.p: budget against the fast tier, never against the pool

span.p: measured

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What has to fit: the Laguna S 2.1 KV cache
2 x 48 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 B = 192.0 KiB per token
24.0 GiB at 128k context, computed from config.json, exact

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
BIOS UMA FB Size - THE KNOB
one boot-time field moves the fast/slow boundary
no discrete GPU exposes this control at all

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
carve-out at the 16 GiB default, the before arm
fast tier ends at a 30 GiB footprint
194.9 GB/s at 30 GiB, 61.3 GB/s at 32 GiB, 114.1 GB/s at 60 GiB
reported pool 82.99 GiB, Windows sees 111.6 GB

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
FAST TIER, carve-out at 96 GB - the planning number
at least 62 GiB, flat at 203-205 GB/s, no knee anywhere swept
a floor, not an edge: the sweep hit the wall below before it found one

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
HARD WALL INSIDE THE FAST TIER - any single tensor at or above 32 GiB
31 GiB copies clean at 199.9 GB/s
32 GiB hard-hangs at 0 CPU, silently, no error, force-killed at 11 min
36 GiB raises hipErrorLaunchFailure

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
SLOWER REGION past the fast tier
reported pool 107.87 GiB, and at least 74.40 GiB written, read back, released
its bandwidth at the 96 GB carve-out is UNMEASURED

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the pool figure is not a ceiling
allocation-only probes returned at least 100 GiB
the driver oversubscribes into system RAM

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
HOST - Windows visible RAM 31.6 GB
the same physical DRAM as the fast tier, with no bus to cross
bandwidth assumed comparable, never measured

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
GPU HBM
TB/s, tens of GiB
size fixed at purchase

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
PCIe
tens of GB/s

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Host DRAM
about 100 GB/s

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
THE RATIO IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT
theirs: 10-50x, set by a bus, not variable
ours: 2-3x, set by a BIOS field, swept in one reboot

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Retention beats eviction as that ratio falls, because a refetch costs
bytes over the slow path and a recompute does not.
So a class of published KV-tiering guidance may be a claim about interconnects
rather than about language models - testable here, and on no card we own.
